key_insight: Neural quantum state training can be reframed as a trust-region reinforcement learning problem, enabling more stable and scalable optimization than standard first-order or SR-style methods.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical optimization recipe for large quantum wavefunction models, especially autoregressive NQS, where exact sampling is cheap but training stability and scalability are bottlenecks.
method: Recast variational energy minimization as an advantage policy-gradient objective over the Born distribution.
Introduce Proximal Wavefunction Optimization (PWO), which clips amplitude probability ratios and phase increments separately.
Reuse samples across multiple updates to improve efficiency while avoiding explicit matrix inversion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved stability and wall-clock convergence on Ising and frustrated J1-J2 spin systems in 1D and 2D, and shows fine-tuning of a 1.5B-parameter RWKV-7 model.
watch_item: PWO still relies on careful trust-region tuning and separate amplitude/phase handling, so implementation details may matter for numerical robustness and reproducibility.
paper_title: One More Time: Revisiting Neural Quantum States from a Reinforcement Learning Perspective
